definitions.gloss: majority vote; majority rule; decision by majority
definitions.explanation: A method of making decisions in which the option supported by more than half of the voters is adopted.

examples.japanese: {多数決|たすうけつ}で{決|き}めよう。
{多数決|たすうけつ}の{結果|けっか}、{旅行先|りょこうさき}はハワイに{決|き}まった。
examples.english: As a result of the majority vote, Hawaii was chosen as the travel destination.

examples.japanese: {多数決|たすうけつ}が{必|かなら}ずしも{正|ただ}しい{結論|けつろん}を{導|みちび}くとは{限|かぎ}らない。
examples.english: A majority vote doesn't necessarily lead to the right conclusion.

notes:
{多数決|たすうけつ} is composed of {多数|たすう} (majority) and {決|けつ} (decision). It refers specifically to the principle or method of deciding by majority.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {多数決|たすうけつ}で{決|き}める (to decide by majority vote)
- {多数決|たすうけつ}を{取|と}る (to take a vote)
- {多数決|たすうけつ}の{原理|げんり} (the principle of majority rule)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {投票|とうひょう}: voting, balloting — the act of casting a vote (broader than majority rule)
- {挙手|きょしゅ}: raising hands — a common method for conducting a {多数決|たすうけつ}
- {全会一致|ぜんかいいっち}: unanimous decision — the opposite approach, requiring all to agree
